\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{امداد} (imdād)}{امداد (imdād)}]{\ur{امداد} (imdād) — aid; relief supplies}

\label{lesson:UR-C299-imdad}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for reassurance, then the Urdu for a reunion.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{امداد}}
\textbf{\ur{امداد}} — \emph{imdād} — \textquotedblleft{}aid; relief supplies\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{حکومت} \ur{نے} \ur{امداد} \ur{بھیجی۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{hukūmat ne imdād bhejī.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The government sent aid.
\end{quote}

Feminine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{امداد}} (\emph{imdād}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{imdād}, \textquotedblleft{}a reinforcing, a supply\textquotedblright{}. It is feminine: \textbf{\ur{امداد} \ur{بھیجی}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{imdād}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{imdād}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hukūmat ne imdād bhejī.} — The government sent aid.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for reassurance, then the Urdu for a reunion, then say \emph{imdād} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{امداد} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Aid; relief supplies\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{رضاکار} (razākār)}{رضاکار (razākār)}]{\ur{رضاکار} (razākār) — a volunteer}

\label{lesson:UR-C299-razakar}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a reunion, then the Urdu for aid.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{رضاکار}}
\textbf{\ur{رضاکار}} — \emph{razākār} — \textquotedblleft{}a volunteer\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{سو} \ur{رضاکار} \ur{گاؤں} \ur{پہنچے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sau razākār gāoṅ pahuṅche.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A hundred volunteers reached the village.
\end{quote}

Masculine or feminine, by the person meant.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{رضاکار}} (\emph{razākār}) is usually traced to Persian \emph{razākār}, built from Arabic \emph{riḍā}, \textquotedblleft{}consent\textquotedblright{}, and Persian \emph{-kār}, \textquotedblleft{}one who does\textquotedblright{}: one who works by choice.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{razākār}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{razākār}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sau razākār gāoṅ pahuṅche.} — A hundred volunteers reached the village.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a reunion, then the Urdu for aid, then say \emph{razākār} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{رضاکار} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A volunteer\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{جمع} \ur{کرنا} (jama karnā)}{جمع کرنا (jama karnā)}]{\ur{جمع} \ur{کرنا} (jama karnā) — to collect; to gather (things)}

\label{lesson:UR-C299-jama-karna}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for aid, then the Urdu for a volunteer.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{جمع} \ur{کرنا}}
\textbf{\ur{جمع} \ur{کرنا}} — \emph{jama karnā} — \textquotedblleft{}to collect; to gather (things)\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{بچوں} \ur{نے} \ur{کپڑے} \ur{جمع} \ur{کیے۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{bachchoṅ ne kapṛe jama kiye.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The children collected clothes.
\end{quote}

Past, with \ur{نے} (he or she …): \ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{پیسے} \ur{جمع} \ur{کیے}, \emph{us ne paise jama kiye}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{جمع} \ur{کرنا}} (\emph{jama karnā}) is built from \emph{jama}, usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{jamʿ}, \textquotedblleft{}a gathering together\textquotedblright{}, and \textbf{\ur{کرنا}}. The things gathered agree: \textbf{\ur{کپڑے} \ur{جمع} \ur{کیے}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jama karnā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jama karnā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bachchoṅ ne kapṛe jama kiye.} — The children collected clothes.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for aid, then the Urdu for a volunteer, then say \emph{jama karnā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{جمع} \ur{کرنا} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To collect; to gather (things)\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{حوصلہ} (hauslā)}{حوصلہ (hauslā)}]{\ur{حوصلہ} (hauslā) — courage; morale}

\label{lesson:UR-C299-hausla}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for a volunteer, then the Urdu for to collect.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{حوصلہ}}
\textbf{\ur{حوصلہ}} — \emph{hauslā} — \textquotedblleft{}courage; morale\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{رضاکاروں} \ur{نے} \ur{لوگوں} \ur{کا} \ur{حوصلہ} \ur{بڑھایا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{razākāroṅ ne logoṅ kā hauslā baṛhāyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The volunteers raised people's spirits.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{حوصلہ}} (\emph{hauslā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ḥawṣala}, \textquotedblleft{}a bird's crop\textquotedblright{}, and so capacity, the room to bear things; in Urdu it is courage. \textbf{\ur{حوصلہ} \ur{بڑھانا}} is to raise someone's spirits.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hauslā}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{hauslā}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{razākāroṅ ne logoṅ kā hauslā baṛhāyā.} — The volunteers raised people's spirits.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Urdu for a volunteer, then the Urdu for to collect, then say \emph{hauslā} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \ur{حوصلہ} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}Courage; morale\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\ur{عطیہ} (atiyā)}{عطیہ (atiyā)}]{\ur{عطیہ} (atiyā) — a donation; a gift}

\label{lesson:UR-C299-atiya}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Urdu for to collect, then the Urdu for morale.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \ur{عطیہ}}
\textbf{\ur{عطیہ}} — \emph{atiyā} — \textquotedblleft{}a donation; a gift\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\ur{اس} \ur{نے} \ur{کیمپ} \ur{کو} \ur{عطیہ} \ur{دیا۔}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{us ne kaimp ko atiyā diyā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
He gave a donation to the camp.
\end{quote}

Masculine.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\ur{عطیہ}} (\emph{atiyā}) is usually traced, through Persian, to Arabic \emph{ʿaṭiyya}, \textquotedblleft{}a gift\textquotedblright{}. It is masculine: \textbf{\ur{عطیہ} \ur{دیا}}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}

\section[(dialogue)]{Looking back: from The Storm to Lending a Hand}

\label{lesson:UR-R299-review-292-299}



\begin{quote}
Say the Urdu for darkness and to thunder.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{Your turn}
Say these aloud:

\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item darkness, to thunder, to flash, destruction, an effect
  \item a village, to flow, to sink, a wave, a whirlpool
  \item a famine, going without food, an epidemic, to rot, cholera
  \item to be trapped, to call out (to), a dead silence, to pull out, in a sorry state
  \item deliverance, a helicopter, to set free, to dart, safe and sound
  \item a relief camp, relief, a tent, refuge, affected
  \item to be separated, to lose one's way, missing, reassurance, a reunion
  \item aid, a volunteer, to collect, morale, a donation
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
Darkness? (\textbf{\ur{اندھیرا}}, \emph{andherā}.) To thunder? (\textbf{\ur{گرجنا}}, \emph{garajnā}.) To flash? (\textbf{\ur{چمکنا}}, \emph{chamaknā}.) Destruction? (\textbf{\ur{تباہی}}, \emph{tabāhī}.) An effect? (\textbf{\ur{اثر}}, \emph{asar}.) A village? (\textbf{\ur{گاؤں}}, \emph{gāoṅ}.) To flow? (\textbf{\ur{بہنا}}, \emph{bahnā}.) To sink? (\textbf{\ur{ڈوبنا}}, \emph{ḍūbnā}.) A wave? (\textbf{\ur{لہر}}, \emph{lahar}.) A whirlpool? (\textbf{\ur{بھنور}}, \emph{bhanvar}.) A famine? (\textbf{\ur{قحط}}, \emph{qahat}.) Going without food? (\textbf{\ur{فاقہ}}, \emph{fāqā}.) An epidemic? (\textbf{\ur{وبا}}, \emph{vabā}.) To rot? (\textbf{\ur{سڑنا}}, \emph{saṛnā}.) Cholera? (\textbf{\ur{ہیضہ}}, \emph{haizā}.) To be trapped? (\textbf{\ur{پھنسنا}}, \emph{phansnā}.) To call out (to)? (\textbf{\ur{پکارنا}}, \emph{pukārnā}.) A dead silence? (\textbf{\ur{سناٹا}}, \emph{sannāṭā}.) To pull out? (\textbf{\ur{نکالنا}}, \emph{nikālnā}.) In a sorry state? (\textbf{\ur{بے} \ur{حال}}, \emph{be hāl}.) Deliverance? (\textbf{\ur{نجات}}, \emph{najāt}.) A helicopter? (\textbf{\ur{ہیلی} \ur{کاپٹر}}, \emph{helī kāpṭar}.) To set free? (\textbf{\ur{چھڑانا}}, \emph{chhuṛānā}.) To dart? (\textbf{\ur{لپکنا}}, \emph{lapaknā}.) Safe and sound? (\textbf{\ur{سلامت}}, \emph{salāmat}.) A relief camp? (\textbf{\ur{کیمپ}}, \emph{kaimp}.) Relief? (\textbf{\ur{راحت}}, \emph{rāhat}.) A tent? (\textbf{\ur{خیمہ}}, \emph{khaimā}.) Refuge? (\textbf{\ur{پناہ}}, \emph{panāh}.) Affected? (\textbf{\ur{متاثر}}, \emph{mutāsir}.) To be separated? (\textbf{\ur{بچھڑنا}}, \emph{bichhaṛnā}.) To lose one's way? (\textbf{\ur{بھٹکنا}}, \emph{bhaṭaknā}.) Missing? (\textbf{\ur{گمشدہ}}, \emph{gumshudā}.) Reassurance? (\textbf{\ur{تسلی}}, \emph{tasallī}.) A reunion? (\textbf{\ur{ملاپ}}, \emph{milāp}.) Aid? (\textbf{\ur{امداد}}, \emph{imdād}.) A volunteer? (\textbf{\ur{رضاکار}}, \emph{razākār}.) To collect? (\textbf{\ur{جمع} \ur{کرنا}}, \emph{jama karnā}.) Morale? (\textbf{\ur{حوصلہ}}, \emph{hauslā}.) A donation? (\textbf{\ur{عطیہ}}, \emph{atiyā}.)
\end{tcolorbox}
